reading.body:
Riley Ohlson is named on 7 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, all for the AFL-CIO, and all naming bills from 2025 or later.

The structure is narrow and consistent. Seven filings, one firm, one client, and 19 distinct bills spread across them. The bills run across both chambers, with HR and S prefixes appearing in roughly even numbers. Nothing in the record shows a second client or a second firm.

For AI specifically, this is a labor federation's interests being represented on AI legislation, not a technology company's. The bills named are the unit of disclosure here, and they are the only signal of subject matter. The record does not say what position was advocated, what the bills would do, or whether any of them moved.

What the data does not cover is large. It gives no dollar amounts, no lobbying spend, no dates of activity beyond the 2025-or-later floor, and no outcome for any bill. It also flags that a different lobbyist shares the name, so the 7 filings should not be read as a complete picture of anyone named Riley Ohlson.
